items: Returns the first error; `WithContext` also cancels its ctx.

blocks.title: Non-negotiable
items: The sender closes the channel, never the receiver.
Closing from the receive side races in-flight sends and panics.
Never `go` inside a library API the caller cannot stop.
Return a stop func, or take a `context.Context`.
Select on `ctx.Done()` in every loop that can block.
Skipping it leaks the child context until the parent is canceled or the timer fires.
Closing a `done chan struct{}` wakes every receiver at once.
`runtime.Gosched()` yields voluntarily — almost never needed now.
Its presence in code usually marks a hidden bug.

blocks.title: Graceful shutdown order
blocks.text: Close the input channel, `Wait` for workers, then close outputs. A hard `os.Exit` skips every deferred cleanup in every goroutine.

blocks.title: A goroutine leak is a memory leak
blocks.text: It holds its stack, its captured variables, and everything those reference. Ten thousand leaked handlers pin ten thousand request bodies.

caption.text: Every goroutine you start needs an owner who can stop it, or it outlives your request. Part 4 of GO GOROUTINES covers errgroup, the context rules that make cancellation work, picking the right primitive, and shutting down cleanly. Save it for the next time your goroutine count and memory climb and never come back down.
